title: Portfolio Risk and Return: Part I
overview: Portfolio risk depends on how asset returns move together, not only on the risk of each asset in isolation.
example: Start with an investor objective and constraints, then connect exposures, diversification, and implementation choices.

modules.title: Historical Risk and Return
modules.explanation: Portfolio risk depends on both individual asset volatility and covariance. Diversification improves the feasible risk-return set when correlations are imperfect; the efficient frontier contains portfolios with the highest expected return for each level of risk.
steps: Estimate expected returns, variances, and pairwise covariances consistently.
Calculate portfolio return and variance using weights and cross terms.
Compare feasible portfolios with investor risk tolerance and diversification limits.
modules.check: Explain how historical risk and return changes an analyst's conclusion, including one limitation.
objectives: Explain historical risk and return in plain language and connect it to the reading's central problem.
Apply the analytical decision rule or analytical decision rule with clearly labeled inputs.
Interpret the result, challenge its assumptions, and identify one condition that would change the conclusion.
lesson: Portfolio risk depends on both individual asset volatility and covariance. Diversification improves the feasible risk-return set when correlations are imperfect; the efficient frontier contains portfolios with the highest expected return for each level of risk.

Portfolio management translates an investor's objectives and constraints into exposures, implementation, monitoring, and rebalancing. Risk is a portfolio property because diversification depends on covariance as well as each holding's standalone volatility.
